official.description_text:
Researcher in Sustainable Finance, part-time 50%
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Architecture and Built Environment
Job description
The duties involve working as a researcher, including leading and developing research projects. Responsibilities also include seeking funding for new research projects, supervising doctoral students, providing administrative research support, and coordinating the research group. A key challenge is to develop research within the field of sustainable finance, which is a new and applied area of ​​research.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree
Experience leading research projects
As a person, you have:·
Research expertise
Teaching ability
The ability to work towards research results being utilized in practice.
The ability to inform about research and development work
Experience of developing and leading activities and staff.
Knowledge of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Collaborative abilities
Independence
Preferred qualifications
Experience leading research projects in Sustainable Finance and Investment.
Ability to read and speak Swedish, for the day to day work
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH
.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long.
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid until further notice (permanent post) according to agreement.
The employment begins with a six-month probationary period.

ai.summary: Permanent part-time (50%) researcher position in sustainable finance and investment at KTH's School of Architecture and Built Environment. Role involves leading research projects, seeking funding, doctoral supervision, and coordinating a research group in an emerging applied field.

thematic_fit.rationale: The position is in sustainable finance and investment—a domain with no thematic connection to human-centred immersive systems, spatial learning, or HCI. The researcher's expertise in XR, spatial cognition, and collaborative learning has no relevance to financial systems or sustainability reporting. Domain mismatch is complete.

methodological_fit.rationale: The role emphasizes research leadership, project development, and translation of research to practice—capabilities the researcher is developing through their MSc research and early publication record. However, the methodological foundations (financial analysis, investment strategy, sustainability metrics) are discipline-specific and unrelated to the researcher's quantitative and qualitative user-centred methods. The overlap is in research management, not technical approach.

growth_value.rationale: This permanent position would develop research leadership and funding skills transferable to any academic field. However, it does not close gaps specific to human-centred XR or immersive learning research (e.g., deeper spatial cognition theory, advanced immersive interface design, or large-scale collaborative system evaluation). A researcher in sustainable finance cannot easily transition to leading human-centred XR groups.

strategic_value.rationale: The permanent, independent researcher role at a strong European institution (KTH, Sweden—a preferred country) is strategically appealing for research autonomy and stability. However, establishing independent researcher identity in sustainable finance is a career commitment that locks the researcher out of human-centred XR domains. The timing is problematic: taking a permanent role before completing the MSc and establishing HCI/XR credentials severely limits future pivots. Part-time status (50%) offers some flexibility but does not address the fundamental domain mismatch.

eligibility_flags: Requires completed PhD by application time. Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress, thesis stage). Ineligible until PhD is conferred.
Position requires 'experience leading research projects' and 'research expertise' in sustainable finance and investment. Researcher has no documented background in either.
Preferred qualification: 'ability to read and speak Swedish for day-to-day work.' Researcher profile does not list Swedish language skills.
Role involves 'developing research within the field of sustainable finance, which is a new and applied area.' Researcher has zero background in finance or investment.
risks: Credential gap: requires PhD; researcher holds MSc in progress. Ineligible until thesis completion and conferment.
Domain expertise absent: sustainable finance and investment are new fields to the researcher. Establishing credibility and independence would require years of intensive retraining.

Career lock-in: accepting a permanent independent researcher position in sustainable finance commits the researcher to that field professionally. Transitioning back to HCI/XR later becomes extremely difficult.
Language barrier: Swedish language preference adds friction to on-site integration and group leadership.

Target identity conflict: this role moves the researcher away from all core themes (human-centred XR, spatial learning, collaborative systems). It does not advance doctoral or faculty pathways aligned with the stated target identity.
